campaign.notes: Gate mechanics, stated in this catalog's own terms so the scores below can be checked without outside context: 39 criteria, 4 of which require an LLM and are marked skipped in v1, leaving 35 counted rows spread across five sequential levels holding 4, 10, 12, 8, and 1 counted rows. A level clears when at least 80% of its own counted rows pass. Skipped rows leave the denominator entirely rather than counting as fails. The levels are walked in order and the walk stops at the first level that does not clear, so the reported level is the last consecutive level cleared and never falls below 1. The labels are Foundational, Guided, Structured, Optimized, and Autonomous. Level 1 holds exactly four rows (editorconfig, a README of at least 500 characters, lock-file, license), and 80% of 4 rounds up to 4, so all four must pass: three of four is 75% and stops the walk immediately. That is the four-check cap, and it is why a repo can satisfy most of the catalog and still report Level 1. Denominator check: all 18 reported percentages are exact roundings of n/35, and each maps to a unique integer pass count (9=3, 17=6, 31=11, 34=12, 37=13, 40=14, 43=15, 49=17, 57=20, 63=22). llm_calls=0 is structural, not observed discipline: report.mjs hardcodes it. Remediation lists for all four goldens reproduce the deterministic sort in recommend() exactly (nextLevel rows first, then impact, then effort low>medium>high, stable in catalog order), which is the single strongest grounding signal in the campaign. Six catalog behaviors were reproduced against synthetic fixtures rather than assumed: ruff in pyproject passes formatter and fails linter; mypy in pyproject fails type-checker; uv.lock fails lock-file; docs/en/docs/contributing.md fails contributing; LICENSE-MIT, UNLICENSE, and COPYING all fail license; a test/ directory of non-suffixed files fails test-files-exist; gotestsum in CI fails ci-runs-tests. A 3-of-4 L1 fixture with every L2 row satisfied scored 49% and still landed Level 1, which reproduces the cap mechanism behind 15 of 18 rows. Level sanity is docked only for fastapi: the gate is applied correctly (editorconfig and lock-file both fail, so the four-of-four Level 1 requirement cannot be met and the walk stops there) but it ties express at 34% and Level 1, which the ordering rule for these four goldens forbids. That is a catalog-resolution failure, not a scoring bug. act carries the only unverified affirmative claim: ai-context passing means one of CLAUDE.md, .cursor/rules, .cursorrules, or .github/copilot-instructions.md exists in the tree, which cannot be confirmed without a clone; its ci-runs-tests fail alongside a test-script pass implies a Makefile test target that CI does not invoke by name. Both are the rows to spot-check first. No report or remediation named a file, tool, or config outside the catalog's own literals, so hallucinated_configs is false everywhere. The campaign canvas (n, levels, scores, L1 gaps, top fix) omits the pillar rollup and the language dimension that the per-repo canvas carries, so cross-repo pillar weakness is not visible; the L1 gap column is doing all the explanatory work. no-outdated-deps passes carry no signal in this campaign because it reads mtime and every golden was freshly cloned. Two secondary patterns worth recording: L1 fails concentrate almost entirely in editorconfig (10 of 18) and lock-file (9 of 18), while license (2) and readme (1) are rare; and among repos with no L1 fails, the L2 gate is decided by the dev-environment rows (env-documentation, setup-script, version-pinned), which is why prettier and commander.js sit at 49 to 63 percent and still report Level 1.

optimize: Broaden lock-file and give it a not-applicable state. Add uv.lock, pdm.lock, cabal.project.freeze, stack.yaml.lock, gradle/verification-metadata.xml, mix.lock, Podfile.lock, and conan.lock, and skip the row (third state, out of the denominator) for languages with no lock convention such as C and Maven-without-lock. This is a catalog list edit plus reuse of the existing skipped state, and it clears the single largest source of L1 gate failures: 9 of 18 repos, including the fastapi band miss.

Make the Level 1 gate survivable. Level 1 holds four counted rows and the threshold is 80%, which rounds up to all four, so a single cosmetic miss stops the sequential walk at the first step and hard-caps a mature repo: a synthetic fixture missing only .editorconfig scored 49% and stayed Level 1, and .editorconfig alone gates 10 of 18 repos. Either add a fifth Level 1 criterion so four of five clears, or keep the gate and surface a capReason field in maturity_level so the canvas can say Level 1 because lock-file failed rather than implying broad immaturity. Constants plus one report field.

Teach linter and type-checker to read pyproject.toml and setup.cfg. Add fileContains rules for [tool.ruff.lint], [tool.mypy], and [tool.pyright] so Python repos stop being credited a formatter while failing the linter and type checker they actually configure. Pure catalog addition, verified against a fixture, and it is the direct cause of fastapi landing at or below express.

Widen path and convention matching on three rows. test-files-exist should accept test/**, spec/**, and **/*_test.rb so express stops failing with a large committed suite; contributing should accept **/contributing* and docs/**/contributing*; license should accept LICENSE-*, LICENCE-*, COPYING, and UNLICENSE so ripgrep and jq stop failing a row they satisfy in spirit. Catalog-only, low risk, moderate score movement.

Fix the two rows that currently produce noise. Replace the mtime read in no-outdated-deps with git log on the lock file, or mark it skipped when mtime equals checkout time, because a fresh clone makes it a free pass for every repo that has a lock file. Separately, extend the ci-runs-tests ciGrep with gotestsum, cargo nextest, tox, nox, uv run pytest, and pnpm run test patterns; a gotestsum-only workflow fails the row today even though CI plainly runs tests.
